 Three weather systems to bring scattered rains, thunderstorms across PH
 jeanette gregorio November 19, 2026 November 19, 2026 0 2 mins 
 MANILA, Philippines — Three weather systems are expected to bring scattered rains and thunderstorms to several parts of the country on Thursday, November 19, 2026, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA).
 In its 5 a.m. weather forecast, the state weather bureau identified the shear line, Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), and easterlies as the weather systems influencing conditions in different parts of the Philippines.
 The shear line, where cold and warm winds converge, may bring cloudy skies, scattered rains, and isolated thunderstorms to affected areas of Luzon.
 Meanwhile, the ITCZ, a region where winds from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres meet, is expected to generate rain showers and thunderstorms in portions of Mindanao.
 The easterlies, or warm and humid winds coming from the Pacific Ocean, may also cause cloudy skies and occasional rainfall in parts of the country.
 PAGASA warned that thunderstorms could produce heavy downpours, potentially triggering flash floods and landslides in vulnerable communities.
 Residents in low-lying and mountainous areas were advised to remain vigilant, particularly during periods of intense rainfall.
 The weather bureau also reminded the public to take precautions against sudden thunderstorms and monitor official weather advisories for possible changes in weather conditions.
